# Jeremiah 32 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The-word which came to Jeremiah from-YHWH in-the-tenth year of-Zedekiah king-of Judah — it [was] the-eighteenth year of-Nebuchadnezzar.

**2** And-at-that-time [the]-army-of the-king-of Babylon was-besieging Jerusalem, and-Jeremiah the-prophet was-shut-up in-the-court-of the-guard which [was] in-the-house-of the-king-of Judah,

**3** Where Zedekiah king-of Judah had-shut-him-up, saying, "Why do-you prophesy, saying, 'Thus says YHWH: Behold-Me giving this city into-the-hand-of the-king-of Babylon, and-he-will-take-it'?"

**4** And-Jeremiah spoke-of the-purchase-of the-field in-Anathoth, as-a-sign that houses and-fields and-vineyards would-again-be-bought in-this-land.

**44** Fields they-will-buy for-money, and-write in-the-deed and-seal and-take witnesses, in-[the]-land-of Benjamin and-in-[the]-surroundings-of Jerusalem and-in-[the]-cities-of Judah and-in-[the]-cities-of the-hill-country and-in-[the]-cities-of the-lowland and-in-[the]-cities-of the-Negev, for I-will-restore their-fortunes," declares YHWH.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **32:1-2**: The precise dating places this during the final siege of Jerusalem (588-586 BCE). Jeremiah is imprisoned for his prophesying yet continues to receive and obey divine commands.

- **32:9**: Sheva sheqalim va-asarah ha-kesef — 'seventeen shekels of silver.' The seemingly trivial purchase price underscores the prophetic sign-act: buying worthless land demonstrates faith in restoration.

- **32:44**: The scope of future restoration: Benjamin, Jerusalem, hill country, Shephelah, Negev — encompasses the entire territory of Judah, not merely the capital.

— EMET
